name: recruitment-inhibited
title: Intervention: block the response

purpose.question:
If the chemotactic response is blocked (lambda -> 0) while the cue is still
secreted, is recruitment abolished?

report.title: Intervention: blocking the response abolishes recruitment
report.objective: Repeat the baseline CPM recruitment world with responder chemotaxis strength set to zero (the intervention) and measure the recruitment index over 500 MC sweeps across 5 seeds.
report.conclusion: Blocking the response abolishes recruitment: the recruitment index stays at 0.000 ± 0.000 across 5 seeds despite the cue being present, versus 0.767 ± 0.170 for the baseline (Cohen's d = 6.38).
report.main_insight: Recruitment is causally dependent on the chemotactic response, not merely on the presence of the cue — the response is a necessary ingredient.
report.caveat: This is a negative control, not an independent positive result: it isolates the response as a necessary cause by removing it, and only has meaning alongside the baseline it is compared to.

study_card.goal: negative control: response blocked abolishes recruitment
study_card.mechanism: Identical CPM world to the baseline except responder chemotaxis lambda = 0 (cue still secreted).
study_card.why_before_next: Isolates the response as a necessary cause — pairs with the adversarial arm to establish both ingredients are required.
study_card.expected_result: Recruitment index stays at (or near) zero for the whole run; no net approach.
study_card.main_expert_question: Does blocking the response (rather than the cue) fully account for the loss of recruitment, ruling out a cue-only explanation?

question:
If the chemotactic response is blocked (lambda -> 0) while the cue is still
secreted, is recruitment abolished?
hypothesis:
With the cue present but the response inhibited, responders no longer climb the
gradient; the recruitment index stays near zero.
objective:
Repeat the baseline world with the responder chemotaxis strength set to zero (the
intervention) and measure the recruitment index over 500 MC sweeps.
description:
The intervention arm of the slice. The world is identical to the baseline except
the responder chemotaxis lambda is set to 0 — the CPM analogue of pharmacologically
blocking the receptor/response while the cue is unchanged. This is the claim
layer's "intervention on the response" made concrete: same cue, blocked response.
claim:
Blocking the chemotactic response abolishes recruitment: the recruitment index
stays at 0 (mean approach ~0), despite the cue being present.
expected_behavior: Recruitment index stays at (or near) zero for the whole run.
Responder mean distance to the source does not fall.

behavior_tests.name: Blocking the response abolishes recruitment
behavior_tests.description:
Pass criterion: recruitment index stays below 0.1 throughout. Measured from the
run: recruitment index remains 0.000 across all 500 sweeps (mean approach -0.08,
i.e. no net approach).

evidence.observed: recruitment index 0.000 ± 0.000 across 5 seeds despite the cue present (baseline 0.767; d=6.38)

controls.name: No cue yields no recruitment (recruitment-adversarial)
controls.description: The other necessary-cause arm — no cue also gives no recruitment.

alternative_hypotheses.claim: Recruitment persists on the cue alone, independent of the response strength.
alternative_hypotheses.note: Excluded here — with the cue present but lambda=0, recruitment is 0.

conclusion:
Recruitment is causally dependent on the chemotactic response, not merely on the
presence of the cue. Together with the baseline, this isolates the response as a
necessary cause.

regression_compatibility.basis: Reproduces the expected abolished-recruitment behaviour with the declared energies and ICs (lambda=0).

explanatory_gain.basis: Isolates the chemotactic response as a necessary ingredient for recruitment.

biological_summary:
This is the response-blocked negative-control arm of the chemotactic-recruitment
slice. The world is identical to the baseline — source cells still secrete the
diffusible cue and form the same spatial gradient — except the responder
chemotaxis strength (lambda) is set to zero, the CPM analogue of pharmacologically
blocking the response. With no bias on their Cellular Potts copy attempts,
responder centres of mass do not drift toward the source and the recruitment
index stays at 0.000 across all 500 Monte-Carlo sweeps and all 5 seeds, versus
0.767 for the baseline. This shows the chemotactic response — not merely the
presence of the cue — is a necessary ingredient for recruitment.

literature_anchors.expectation: Blocking the chemotactic response abolishes gradient-directed recruitment even when the cue is present.

key_assumptions: Identical world to recruitment-baseline except responder chemotaxis lambda = 0.

model_change.notes:
Same parameterized CPMProcess as the baseline, with chemo_lambda forced to 0
(response blocked) while cue_rate is unchanged (cue present). No new
processes, state variables, or listeners were added.

design_pivot_required.question: Should the response-blocked condition be built as a dedicated study arm, or treated only as an implicit zero-baseline comparison?
alternatives: Treat lambda=0 as an informal baseline comparison only
Build a dedicated inhibited study as a first-class necessary-ingredient control (this study)
design_pivot_required.notes:
Resolved by building this as its own study: it isolates the chemotactic
response as a necessary cause, excluding "the cue alone suffices" as an
alternative explanation, and gives the investigation causal (not just
correlational) evidence for the recruitment claim.
